[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on a medium shot along a shallow ditch in the heather at a soldier lying flat in it on his elbows with a long pole in both hands and a white flag on the end of it up above the spoil, the raw sand ring of the pit far off standing quiet and unanswering far beyond him. The camera is at the lip of the ditch level with the spoil, five paces from him, a 50mm lens. A hard high sun stands at the RIGHT. At the first frame the soldier lies along the ditch across the BOTTOM third from the LEFT third to the CENTRE, the pole rising from his hands to the white flag at the CENTRE RIGHT. The raw sand ring of the pit stands far off in the TOP third at the CENTRE. The shot is inside this place: the sand-pits on Horsell Common on a hot bright afternoon in 1894: the raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater, a single continuous streamer of grey smoke standing straight up out of it in the air, knee-deep heather and dark furze running away flat to a horizon of low pines. The camera tracks sideways to the right along the ditch, a truck with small amplitude, until the ring of sand already in the picture is at the centre as he goes on swinging the pole from side to side above the spoil through a hand’s breadth, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 the flag goes on turning over on itself as it swings, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
